title: Restriction commutes with list conjunction
statement: Let $f_1, \dots, f_k$ be Boolean functions on $n$ variables and let $\rho$ be a restriction of those variables, and write $f|_\rho$ for the restriction of a function $f$ along $\rho$ (the function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$). Then restricting the pointwise conjunction $f_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge f_k$ along $\rho$ agrees, at every point $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}$, with the pointwise conjunction of the individually restricted functions $f_1|_\rho, \dots, f_k|_\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: a finite list of Boolean functions on n variables
a restriction rho on the n variables
equality holds at every point x
replaced:
Restricting the pointwise AND of a list of functions equals the pointwise AND of the
restricted functions: for all $x$, $\mathrm{restrictFn}\,(\mathrm{listAnd}\,fs)\,\rho\,x =
\mathrm{listAnd}(fs.\mathrm{map}\,(\lambda f.\ \mathrm{restrictFn}\, f\,\rho))\,x$.
